candidate_093_component_decomposition.name: physics-outcome-conditioned slip-to-forbid repair — component attribution correction
candidate_093_component_decomposition.source: Official AdsMind author repository matched ablation summaries plus arXiv:2606.19152v1.

candidate_093_component_decomposition.interpretation: The new component tables materially narrow candidate_093. Full-vs-1-Shot strongly supports repeated physics-grounded closed-loop evaluation, but neither explicit FORBID nor the combined Slip+associated-FORBID knockout shows a significant directional energy penalty relative to Full on these matched benchmarks. Therefore the earlier mechanism-specific attribution to slip-to-forbid repair is downgraded: the observed system advantage cannot currently be assigned causally to FORBID or Chemical Slip alone. The previously observed 0.99 eV over-constraint case remains a direct warning against irreversible prohibitions.
candidate_093_component_decomposition.scope_guard: Do not infer that Slip/FORBID are useless outside these benchmarks or for interpretability/safety; the result is only that minimum-energy benchmark performance does not show an isolated positive causal effect here.

candidate_094.name: gate-activation coverage before guardrail credit
candidate_094.mechanism_hypothesis: A validator/safety gate should receive causal reliability credit only after the evaluation suite contains cases that actually activate it; report gate-fire coverage and include targeted challenge cases, otherwise a dormant guard may look successful merely because the benchmark never exercised it.

primary_evidence.source: Official AdsMind per-agent ablation diagnostics in the author repository.
primary_evidence.result: On CMU20, no_validator has 100% success, identical to Full. validator_rejections are zero for every backend/variant combination. The authors' diagnostic README states that, together with 1,240 additional OCD62 runs, the validator never fired in the paper's experiments and is architectural insurance rather than active machinery on these benchmarks.
primary_evidence.executor_control: In the same CMU20 per-agent ablation, bypassing the MACE executor yields MAE versus Full of 2.416 eV (GPT-5.4), 2.005 eV (Claude 4.6), 1.453 eV (Gemini 2.5), and 2.025 eV (Grok-4.3), far larger than the per-backend MAE-versus-Full values for no_slip/no_forbid/no_termination in the same table. This supports the narrower claim that physics execution is active and outcome-determining for reproducing the Full workflow, while the validator is untested as an active guard in this benchmark corpus.
primary_evidence.limits: This is negative/coverage evidence, not proof that validators are unnecessary. The DFT overlap is only six cases and should not be used to infer physical accuracy of no_executor; the comparison here is to Full behavior and observed gate activation.

wet_lab_ablation_search.source: ProtoPilot, arXiv:2606.31763v2 and fresh public search.
wet_lab_ablation_search.result: ProtoPilot explicitly connects execution observations to state update, replanning and targeted protocol revision, and reports 96.6% overall gate pass across 294 tasks plus physical feedback-corrected PCA assembly. Targeted searches did not surface a matched component ablation that removes only runtime skill evolution, rubric validation, or wet-lab feedback while holding the rest fixed. It remains system-level supporting evidence rather than causal evidence for a specific gate/self-evolution mechanism.
